pitfalls.name: Creating unconnected ontology elements
pitfalls.description: Ontology elements (classes, object properties and datatype properties) are created isolated, with no relation to the rest of the ontology.

pitfalls.name: Defining wrong inverse relationships
pitfalls.description: Two relationships are defined as inverse relations when they are not necessarily inverse.

pitfalls.name: Missing annotations
pitfalls.description: This pitfall consists in creating an ontology element and failing to provide human readable annotations attached to it. Consequently, ontology elements lack annotation properties that label them (e.g. rdfs:label, lemon:LexicalEntry, skos:prefLabel or skos:altLabel) or that define them (e.g. rdfs:comment or dc:description). This pitfall is related to the guidelines provided in [5].

pitfalls.name: Defining multiple domains or ranges in properties
pitfalls.description: The domain or range (or both) of a property (relationships and attributes) is defined by stating more than one rdfs:domain or rdfs:range statements. In OWL multiple rdfs:domain or rdfs:range axioms are allowed, but they are interpreted as conjunction, being, therefore, equivalent to the construct owl:intersectionOf. This pitfall is related to the common error that appears when defining domains and ranges described in [7].

pitfalls.name: Misusing ontology annotations
pitfalls.description: The contents of some annotation properties are swapped or misused. This pitfall might affect annotation properties related to natural language information (for example, annotations for naming such as rdfs:label or for providing descriptions such as rdfs:comment). Other types of annotation could also be affected as temporal, versioning information, among others.

pitfalls.name: Using different naming conventions in the ontology
pitfalls.description: The ontology elements are not named following the same convention (for example CamelCase or use of delimiters as "-" or "_") . Some notions about naming conventions are provided in [2].

pitfall_names: Defining multiple domains or ranges in properties
Using different naming conventions in the ontology
